title: Additive value of polygenic risk and family history for coronary heart disease risk stratification in two diverse US cohorts.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: no open-access full text in Europe PMC, no supplement, no accessions, no Zenodo/Dryad hits; only an NCBI link to a PMC record (13504335), whose Europe PMC lookup returned nothing usable.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract: participant-level data come from eMERGE (Electronic Medical Records and Genomics) phase IV (n = 19,348) and All of Us (n = 239,645). Both are controlled-access human genotype plus health-record resources (eMERGE via dbGaP/AnVIL application; All of Us via registered Researcher Workbench), so no open download is expected.

a1_downloadable.note: Individual-level genotypes, family history and coronary heart disease outcomes sit in controlled-access cohorts (eMERGE IV via dbGaP application, All of Us via registered Researcher Workbench with data-use agreement). Flag: controlled access. No open file found in the paper record or repositories.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked in files; inside the cohorts coronary heart disease status would be derived from health-record codes, so it is constructed, not measured directly.

a5_enough_rows.note: Paper text only: 19,348 plus 239,645 participants; not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not checked; All of Us analysis must run in its cloud workbench anyway.

honest_claim_h3: Not reachable: data are controlled access, so no claim can be tested locally.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use inherited genetic risk scores, family history and standard clinical risk factors to predict who develops coronary heart disease.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-person polygenic risk score, familial hypercholesterolemia variant status, family history and clinical risk factors; about 259,000 people per the abstract (unverified).
plain_idea.predict: Whether a person has or develops coronary heart disease (heart attack, unstable angina or artery-opening procedure), taken from electronic health records.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cardiologists and guideline writers would learn whether adding genetics and family history improves risk calculators across racial/ethnic groups; but the paper already answers this with regression models.

ml_idea: Not pursued: tabular risk prediction on controlled-access cohort data; it would require dbGaP and All of Us access and cloud workbench compute, outside the laptop-only, open-data scope.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether any open, individual-level table was deposited: none found (no supplement, no accessions, no repository hits).

verdict_reason: A1 fails: all participant-level data are controlled access (eMERGE IV through a dbGaP application, All of Us through a registered cloud workbench). No open download exists, and the paper itself is not open access.
